Sample.evidence_source: The entire section describes a single individual, Sam, and his experiences leading to his death.

Population.evidence_source: Sam was described by his parents as a high flyer with an extraordinary mind. ... He died at the age of 20, shortly before he was due to return for his second year at university.

Type.evidence_source: Sam was described by his parents as a high flyer with an extraordinary mind. ... His parents observed how he lost all confidence when he went to university. ... During his first year at university, two major events of note contributed to his psychological distress. First, in examining the events that led up to Sam's death, his parents identified his dissatisfaction with academic progress as a major point of frustration: ... Second, Sam had a relationship with a female student which was described as intensely emotional and turbulent. ... Sam's sibling recalls a telephone conversation with him approximately 2 weeks before his death. ... Letters written by him shortly before his death reveal he was consumed with self-doubt...

Area.evidence_source: his parents recall the onset of depression at around the age of 14. They remember noticeable mood swings at that point (used to be high—energetic and creative—and he used to be low). ... he lost all confidence when he went to university. It seems university life didn't match up to his expectations and he became disillusioned. During this time, he experienced intense doubts about his ability to succeed in his course, severe doubts about his ability to hold a relationship together, and suffered disappointments of different kinds (where he over-reacted to making mistakes). ... his parents identified his dissatisfaction with academic progress as a major point of frustration: ... Sam's perception that the breakdown of two relationships meant he was a social failure is indicative of the dichotomous (all or nothing) thinking common among perfectionists. ... This, in turn, triggered periods of anxiety and depression; it turned the high hopes and expectations he had for himself and others to disillusionment, frustration, and despair. ... He said he felt depressed. Letters written by him shortly before his death reveal he was consumed with self-doubt, and had become highly self-critical and disillusioned...
